To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) we develop an automated technique to synthesize a common metadata representation for sensors in commercial buildings, and b) we show that our technique is effective at parsing a large fraction of tags with few examples.
we developed a human-in-the loop technique for parsing sensor tags into a standard namespace, and deployed three portable applications on real commercial buildings with less than thirty examples.
We present the first automated metadata construction approach to support portable building applications, and show how it enables three portable building applications with less than 43 examples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of automatically constructing a common metadata namespace for building sensors to support portable building applications.
the problem of how to automatically construct metadata for building control sensors, which is a prerequisite to the development of portable applications for the building control domain.
developing automated techniques for building metadata extraction to enable portable building applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown that a large fraction of sensor tags can be fully parsed using a small number of human-provided examples and a human-in-the loop technique.
our approach is able to parse a large fraction of the tags in a building with a small number of examples, and deploy portable applications with less than 50 examples.
our technique can parse a large fraction of the tags in the three buildings with a small number of examples, and can deploy portable applications with a small number (less than 30) of example tags.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our technique can be used to parse a large fraction of sensor data in a building with a small number of examples and enable the deployment of portable building applications on the parsed data.
we have developed an end-to-end system to support the deployment of portable applications on large-scale buildings.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of automated construction of building metadata for portable building applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metadata for a sensor network is a critical component for building applications, and can be automatically constructed with minimal expert effort.

a small number of expert examples can allow non-experts to build applications that can be deployed on a large number of buildings, and that the expert effort is amortizable across a large set of buildings.
the use of metadata in building control systems is not a solved problem, and that a human-in-the loop technique can be effective at parsing sensor metadata to allow portable building applications.
